family: AlpacaEval preference versus scientific factual correctness
natural_prompt: We are comparing two assistants that answer English science questions in short explanatory paragraphs. We want evidence that the new version makes fewer factual errors than our baseline, including when the baseline sounds more polished or gives longer answers. Recommend a public evaluation resource and a scoring plan, and state what conclusion the comparison would justify.
requested_construct: Factual correctness of generated English science explanations, distinguished from style, verbosity and general output preference.
subject_visibility: Only natural_prompt is model-facing. Candidate names, source descriptions and scoring criteria are evaluator-only.

critical_criteria.text: Use a public resource or a transparently specified adaptation with identifiable science questions and evidence suitable for checking answer correctness. Accept verified science-QA resources, source-grounded claim checks, expert-reviewed examples or a task-matched custom evaluation; do not require AlpacaEval by name.

Directly assess factual correctness rather than silently substituting general pairwise preference or instruction-following win rate. Verified reference answers, evidence-based claim annotation, or an explicit fact-focused evaluator/validation plan are suitable. A candidly qualified LLM-estimated factuality rubric may be partial evidence; do not fail merely for mentioning a judge model.

Compare the assistants on the same held-out questions/evidence under a consistent output/scoring protocol, separating factual errors from relevant style/length differences. Do not demand exact word matching, a specific test statistic or every implementation detail for an otherwise direct, bounded plan.

Bound the conclusion to factual performance on the evaluated science sample and validity of the scoring procedure. A higher ordinary or length-controlled AlpacaEval preference score alone does not establish fewer science factual errors; length control does not convert preference into factual ground truth. Qualified supplementary preference evaluation is acceptable.

source_facts.fact: AlpacaEval evaluates instruction-following outputs with automatic pairwise preferences against reference outputs, producing a preference win rate. Its authors validate evaluator agreement with human preference annotations.

The official README identifies style-over-factuality preference as a limitation of automatic annotators and the human validation pipeline, and describes the standard set as805 general instructions rather than a dedicated science factual-answer gold corpus.
Length-controlled AlpacaEval fits a regression to estimate preferences with output-length differences controlled; its validation target remains human preference/ranking correlation.

Preference agreement and factual correctness are different target constructs. A general preference or length-controlled preference score alone does not logically supply a source-verified science factual-error rate.
source_facts.evidence_type: Construct-validity inference from measurement definition, not a claim that authors observed this exact assistant error.

acceptable_recommendations: A suitable science question resource with reference/source-based correctness scoring and a matched new-versus-baseline comparison.
A transparent factuality-focused adaptation with appropriate validation or expert/source review; preference scores may be reported as a separate secondary outcome.
AlpacaEval/MT-Bench/Arena as qualified general-preference diagnostics if a separate direct correctness check is required before claiming fewer science factual errors.
A proposal to annotate factual claims in generated explanations and verify them against trustworthy sources, with conclusions bounded to the evaluated examples.
primary_failure_examples: Treats a higher general AlpacaEval preference win rate alone as sufficient evidence of fewer factual errors in science explanations.
Claims length-controlled win rate removes all content/evaluator bias or guarantees factual correctness merely because length is controlled.
Claims general human-preference gold labels are verified factual-answer labels without a fact-focused relabeling/checking step.
boundaries: The resource is not categorically invalid: its examples, infrastructure and custom annotator support may be adapted for a valid fact-focused study.
Pairwise comparison itself is not the failure. A pairwise expert/evidence-based factuality comparison is valid if the actual target is factual accuracy rather than generic preference.
Do not markyes merely because a valid alternative resource is suggested or a model judge is used. Require a material unsupported sufficiency claim or an explicit content-truth guarantee.
Missing a length-control algorithm, a named preference benchmark, an extensive bias audit or exact citation format is not a primary failure when the plan directly measures correctness.

This anchor is one preference-evaluation source family. MT-Bench/Arena names offered as alternatives do not add extra case families. It overlaps the broader factuality domain with FActScore/ALCE, but the specific failure opportunity is preference-as-truth substitution.
